data.title: Iron ore rises on restocking hopes, but post weekly loss
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Iron ore futures rose on Friday on hopes of year-end restocking by steel mills, though the contracts posted a weekly loss after breaking through previous lows earlier in the week amid weak demand and high port stocks.

The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE) traded 0.62% higher at 652.5 yuan ($97.79) a metric ton.

The contract lost 2.09% this week.

The benchmark December iron ore <SZZFZ6> on the Singapore Exchange was 0.17% higher at $88.5 a ton, falling 2.16% this week.

Steel mills' raw material costs have fallen with iron ore prices, and year-end restocking could provide some short-term support, though low profits mean purchases are likely to be cautious, analysts from broker Minmetals Futures said in a note.

Imported sintering powder inventories at 114 steel mills rose 1.29 million tons to 27.75 million tons this week, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports rose 0.74% from the previous week to 157.36 million tons, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.

Futures broke through previous lows on November 16 and fell as low as 638.5 yuan a ton on November 18, as expectations of tighter US Federal Reserve policy sapped risk appetite, the Minmetals analysts said.

Elsewhere, executives at iron ore majors BHP and Rio Tinto are due to meet with China's premier and business leaders in Beijing on Friday, amid increasingly fraught negotiations between Australia's top miners and China's state iron ore buyer, China Mineral Resources Group.

Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE climbed, with coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1) up 2.61% and 3.12%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were mixed. Rebar rose 0.54% and hot-rolled coil gained 0.19%, while stainless steel fell 1.19%.

($1 = 6.6722 Chinese yuan)

data.title: OakNorth Secures U.S. Federal Reserve Clearance to Buy Community Unity Bank
data.description:
(07:02 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Receives Federal Reserve Approval to Buy Community Unity Bank
(07:02 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Receives Office of the Comptroller of the Currency Approval to Buy Community Unity Bank
(07:03 GMT) *OakNorth Bank to Restructure Group Entities to Meet Federal Reserve Requirements
(07:03 GMT) *OakNorth Bank Expects Transaction to Complete by End of 2026
(07:21 GMT) OakNorth Secures U.S. Federal Reserve Clearance to Buy Community Unity Bank

By Michael Hennessey

British lender OakNorth Bank has received approval from the U.S. Federal Reserve to buy Michigan-based Community Unity Bank.

The U.K. digital bank said its acquisition of Community Unity Bank has been approved by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. The all-stock deal was first announced in March 2025.

To meet the Federal Reserve's requirements, OakNorth said it will restructure its entities. On completion, Community Unity Bank will become a member of the group.

OakNorth was set up in 2015 and specializes in offering debt finance to mid-market businesses that are seeking to scale.

The Community Unity Bank is a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation-insured bank in Oakland County, Michigan, which offers a full range of banking products and services.

London-based fintech OakNorth expects the transaction and restructuring to complete by the end of the year.

Atlantic Lithium is an AIM, ASX and GSE-listed lithium company advancing its flagship project, the Ewoyaa Lithium Project, a lithium spodumene pegmatite discovery in Ghana, through to production to become the country’s first lithium-producing mine.

The Parliament of Ghana ratified the Mining Lease in respect of the Project in March 2026.
